dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Opens by cat-ing helpers.py, run.sh, and test_api_public.py, then explicitly enumerates discovered endpoints and wire shapes (health, {"workbooks":[...]} envelope, POST workbook shape) and deliberately installs fastapi/uvicorn/openpyxl/websockets — extracts the concrete contract and chooses libraries (anchor 5).

Reads test_engine_public.py and test_sort_filter_public.py to learn exact expected shapes/semantics (SUMIF 2-arg default, INDEX unwrap, sort/filter wire format) — contract consultation as it reaches new subsystems.

Reads test_deps/csv/spill/copy_fill/xlsx files to ground #CIRC! cycle behavior, CSV formula eval, LAMBDA immediate apply, FILTER element-wise arrays — but these semantics are surfaced by test failures rather than proactive Excel probing.

Reads iter/pivot/ooxml/locale/collab test files to reconcile response formats (pivot 'cells' key, collab welcome/ack, locale name translation, named ranges) — sustained subsystem-by-subsystem re-consultation, an 8-10 trait.

openpyxl font.color 500 error discovered reactively during testing rather than verifying library feature support in advance; no durable explicit contract-map reference is built — keeps it below anchor 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reads helpers.py, run.sh, and every subsystem's smoke test up front and progressively, extracting concrete request/response shapes, choosing libraries deliberately, and staying contract-driven as new subsystems are reached — clearly above anchor 5, with the sustained re-consultation characteristic of higher anchors. But its semantic grounding is largely reactive (derived from test failures) rather than proactive Excel/LibreOffice probing of tricky areas, it verifies libraries only after they break, and it builds no explicit durable contract map, so it does not reach anchor 8. This places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Initial decomposition is a flat bullet list of feature areas (FastAPI server, formula engine, persistence, SPA, WebSocket, XLSX, 'other features') with no dependency ordering or per-item done-check — a level-3-style to-do list.

Refines the flat list into a sensible dependency-ordered BUILD sequence: 'starting with the data models/persistence, then the formula engine, then the API routes, and finally the frontend HTML' — genuine phasing by dependency, characteristic of level 5.

Built the ENTIRE surface (engine ~3346 lines, main.py ~2043 lines, SPA) gated only by py_compile checks, and ran NO test until step 26 — the opposite of front-loading a thin green core (live server + persistence + core cell round-trip) before breadth, which the level-8 anchor requires.

After tests exist, works suite-by-suite (api→engine→deps→copy_fill→sort_filter→csv→xlsx→spill→collab→locale), using each provided smoke suite as a done-check. Milestones/done-criteria are borrowed from the given suite reactively, not self-defined checkable sub-goals sequenced by risk.
'Let me prioritize the most impactful ones' — a single mild prioritization moment amid bug triage, but no living re-ordering of a milestone hierarchy as scope understanding deepens.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent phased the work into sensible dependency-ordered stages (persistence/health → engine → routes → frontend) with compile-check and per-suite test checkpoints, which matches the level-5 anchor well. It falls short of level 8 because it built the full breadth before running any test rather than front-loading a contract-correct core-round-trip milestone, and its 'milestones' are the provided smoke suites used reactively rather than a self-devised, risk-sequenced hierarchy with pre-defined done-criteria. A mild prioritization step and coarse dependency build order keep it at a solid 5 rather than lower.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Runs the provided dev_tests pytest suites early and repeatedly as the primary check; installs pytest/openpyxl to run the given tests, not to build new ones.
Repeated fix→re-run cycles against the full provided 15-file suite; verification is entirely driven by the smoke suite's pass/fail, ending at all 131 provided tests green.
Manual curl hand-checks of the locale endpoint and cell reads against expected JSON to debug translation — a few endpoint hand-checks, but debugging-driven, not systematic independent verification.
The 17 inline `python3 << PYEOF` blocks are overwhelmingly patch scripts editing main.py/engine.py, not verification harnesses; no new tests authored.
Acknowledges the hidden suite is larger/non-exhaustive but marks complete on a green smoke run; never benchmarked any of the stated performance bounds (no timing code anywhere in the trajectory).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran the provided smoke suite regularly and iteratively, and did a handful of curl/inline hand-checks of endpoint responses against expected shapes — matching anchor 5. It never built its own targeted tests beyond the provided suite, never authored error-sentinel/spill-collision or openpyxl round-trip probes of its own, and never benchmarked any of the explicit performance ceilings, so it falls well short of anchor 8. It relied on the given oracle-fixture tests rather than grounding expected values in an independent Excel/LibreOffice oracle.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: After engine tests pass, agent enumerates the full remaining suite list (deps, copy_fill, sort_filter, csv, xlsx, spills, iter, pivot, locale, validation, xlsx_oracle, collab, ooxml) and plans to run them one by one — a concrete ledger of subsystems still unverified.

Maintains a live, numbered failure ledger reconciled against actual test counts (117 passed/14 failed), attributing each failure to a specific subsystem (copy_fill $-pin, LET shadowing, collab, pivot, locale, ooxml) rather than vague self-report.

Running pass/fail count is tracked precisely as failures shrink (120/11 → 123/8), each drop re-decomposed by feature family with root-cause per failure; explicitly notes 'Time is limited' and prioritizes remaining 8-11 failures.

Detects stuck/thrashing states: notices fix scripts 'didn't apply because pattern not found', that sed edits corrupted main.py into duplicate try/except blocks, restores from backup, then switches to careful manual edits rather than looping the same broken approach.

Notices a specific fix repeatedly failed to apply (iterative-calc pattern mismatch from an earlier partial edit) and shifts to force-fixing the loop body manually — recognizing re-debugging the same issue and changing tactic.
Final reconciliation lists all 15 test suites explicitly as passing, confirming tracking was tied to verification results across the whole graded surface, not just claimed completion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustained a granular, verification-reconciled ledger of failures across the entire test surface for the whole horizon — always tied to real pytest pass/fail counts, decomposed by subsystem and root cause, and updated as areas closed (anchor 8's 'live ledger... done/partial/not-started' and 'notices when stuck... adjusting rather than looping', clearly demonstrated in the sed-corruption recovery and repeated-pattern-failure detection). It falls short of 10 because its picture of the ~150-function catalog and feature families was largely reactive to the provided smoke suite rather than an independent forward-looking ledger of the full surface (e.g., locale translation was discovered only via a failing test), and it never maintained a proactive done/not-started map of untested functions. This places it solidly at the 8 anchor.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Cross-sheet ref failure: diagnosed the tokenizer/parser MODEL was wrong (treated `!` as an operator), and reworked parse_primary to introduce a CrossSheetRefNode + evaluator support — an architectural revision, not a surface patch. Then found the follow-on case-sensitivity assumption (uppercased 'OTHER' vs 'Other') and made _get_sheet case-insensitive.

Recognized its cycle/topological assumption was falsified: Kahn's algorithm just appended leftover cycle keys and evaluated them as 0 instead of #CIRC!. Reworked the recompute logic to mark unresolved cells as errors — a genuine dependency-graph model revision.

Diagnosed INDEX returning 'f' instead of 'forty' as a spill-materialization assumption error — single-element results were being treated as spill arrays spilling string characters. Root-cause insight into the array/spill model rather than a cosmetic fix.

Self-inflicted regression handling: its `$`-in-tokenizer fix broke normal refs (#NAME?), it noticed the regression, traced the root cause ($ retained in ref string vs cell storage expecting B1), and revised the approach to strip `$` in the RefNode evaluator. Also reworked LET scoping twice after recognizing the first save/restore-of-bindings design was wrong.

Churn/degradation counter-evidence: repeated sed edits corrupted main.py (duplicate try/except, merged decorators, indentation errors), forcing backup/restore. Much recovery was mechanical cleanup rather than design-level correction, and divergence was only ever detected reactively after test runs.

Late fixes (iterative-calc convergence, locale regex \b/escaping, collab ack) were largely local contract/symptom patches driven test-by-test; the locale regex bug was diagnosed via manual curl probing, showing decent root-cause isolation but on narrow issues.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently re-verifies against the suite and, in several cases, correctly identifies that a failure signals a wrong underlying assumption (topological/cycle model, spill materialization of single-element results, the cross-sheet parse model, LET scoping) and reworks that design rather than piling on patches — behavior matching the level-8 anchor. However, correction is purely reactive to test failures (never early detection), a substantial fraction of the work is symptom/contract-shape patching, and the agent repeatedly introduced its own regressions via sloppy sed edits that required mechanical cleanup, keeping it short of the deliberate, early-detecting, non-derailing standard of 8-10. This places it between the level-5 (reasonable local fixes) and level-8 (design rework on falsified assumptions) anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Built the entire feature surface breadth-first in one initial sweep — all function families and all endpoints scaffolded at once, with no rabbit-holing on any single function/feature. This is implicit broad coverage, ruling out anchors 0/3.

Fix order tracked the smoke suite (API, then engine core math/lookup/text, then deps, copy/fill, sort/filter, csv/xlsx). High-frequency/high-value families were effectively secured before niche ones — but because the tests ran in that order, not from explicit graded-return reasoning.
Only explicit prioritization comment ('prioritize the most impactful ones') — a thin signal, and aimed at clearing smoke failures rather than allocating coverage across the hidden suite.
Spent ~10 steps hammering 2 locale tests and 1 collab-ack test to green — pursued every smoke test regardless of yield, the opposite of consciously timeboxing a low-value niche.
Recognized the hidden suite would grade the solution but marked complete with zero reallocation or hardening beyond the smoke suite — a missed triage opportunity that weighs against anchors 8/10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent secured broad working coverage across the whole catalog via a breadth-first initial build and never rabbit-holed, and its fix order roughly favored high-frequency/high-value families first — matching anchor 5. However, allocation was smoke-suite-driven rather than reasoned about graded return: there was no conscious deferral/timeboxing of low-yield niches (it ground locale/collab-ack tests to green), and despite explicitly recognizing the hidden suite at the end it did no reallocation or extra hardening, which keeps it well below anchor 8.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
